column1: consistent|accurate|Alei is an attested greeting; the standalone utterance needs no clause.
consistent|accurate|Elora sen is a name followed by the optional neutral-polite address; sen does not mark gender.
consistent|accurate|Elora mel is a name plus intimate address; Turkish canım reflects its warmth, not a gender distinction.
consistent|accurate|Sai is the subject, süli a zero-copula quality and le a polar question marker.
consistent|accurate|Ei answers yes and mei süli is an affirmative zero-copula quality clause.
consistent|accurate|Nai answers no and ne precedes the quality predicate süli.
consistent|accurate|Vena asks location; the zero-copula question has Sai as subject.
consistent|accurate|Lem lo marks location and Mei is the subject; Turkish supplies the copula.
consistent|accurate|Samel is a nominal predicate after Eli; Eli has no grammatical gender.
consistent|accurate|Keli is interrogative subject and da marks past before avelen.
consistent|accurate|Sael-en is the verb and Sai-n the marked object; SVO is neutral.
consistent|accurate|Sai-n precedes Sael-en; SOV gives object focus without changing the basic proposition.
consistent|accurate|El follows the subject as additive focus; Sai-n is the object of saelen.
consistent|accurate|Eral-en is remember and Sai-n is the marked person object.

consistent|accurate|Du marks ongoing action and Añel-en derives the verb dream.
